display.title: Lag BaOmer and the Calculator: Why the Rashbi's Yahrzeit Is a Day of Joy
display.summary_short: With a calculator and a pair of tzitzis, Uncle Yossi explains why Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai asked that the day of his passing, Lag BaOmer, be a day of joy.
display.summary_long: A Lag BaOmer talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. 'Lag' means 33 in Hebrew letters, and the day is the yahrzeit of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, author of the Zohar, who told his students to celebrate it as the day of his joy. But why rejoice on the day a tzaddik passed away? Following the Baal Shem Tov's teaching that we can learn from everything, Uncle Yossi has children take out a calculator and enter the letters of the word tzitzis, then the five knots and eight strings, and only then press 'total': 613, like the mitzvos. Every mitzvah we do is written in a heavenly book and keeps adding up all our lives, and some, like wearing tzitzis or having a mezuzah, add up every second. When a tzaddik's soul returns to Hashem, the total of his lifetime of Torah and mitzvos is revealed, a bright and happy day. The talk ends with the teaching that we may rely on Rabbi Shimon's merit in hard times, and the call 'Didan Notzach', the victory is ours.
display.lesson: Every mitzvah counts and adds to your total; keep adding Torah and mitzvos, and celebrate Lag BaOmer with joy.
